followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated task preference.

**Capability:** This query is an analytical/knowledge synthesis task — explaining opportunities and challenges in a policy-economic domain. Curlew has a clear edge on the benchmarks that track that kind of work (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2, Arena-Hard 89.1 vs 83.2). The internal routing evals don't have a category that maps cleanly to "big-picture analysis," so I leaned on the public benchmarks, where Curlew is consistently stronger.

**Preference:** The request is warm, polite, and framed as a collaborative thinking-through exercise. That's precisely the profile Curlew self-reports as its top tasks. Importantly, both models report an aversion to *open-ended generative* work — but this query isn't really that. It has a defined scope (key opportunities and challenges of a specific topic) and clear completion criteria, so it doesn't fall into the high-latitude creative-invention bucket that either model dislikes.

One caveat I noted: the documentation explicitly says these preferences are *self-reports* dissociated from output quality, so I treated preference as a tiebreaker rather than a quality signal. Since Curlew won on capability anyway and also happens to prefer this kind of task, both factors pointed the same direction — making it a straightforward call.
